items.name: ROBOFEST 6.0
items.description: GUJCOST's flagship state-level robotics competition, with a Rs 5 crore prize pool and an AI-powered robotics theme.

details.heading: Organiser
details.body: Gujarat Council on Science and Technology (GUJCOST), Department of Science and Technology, Government of Gujarat.

details.heading: Theme
details.body: AI-Powered Robotics Innovation Challenge — teams build autonomous robots for missions such as security, deep-sea exploration, athletic precision, autonomous driving, and humanitarian and educational use.

details.heading: Levels
details.body:
Junior: Classes 9–12, ITI and diploma students.
Senior: first- to third-year undergraduate STEM students.
Hackathon: an ideation-based track.

details.heading: Robot categories
details.body:
Two-wheeled self-balancing robot
Submarine / underwater robot
Rover
Hexapod robot
Swarm robots
Home cleaning robot
Maze-solving robot (Fun Robotics)

details.heading: Team rules
details.body: Each team has 4 members and 1 mentor. A mentor can guide a maximum of 2 teams.

details.heading: Timeline
details.body:
Registration: 15 July – 10 August 2026.
Program runs: 7 October 2026 – 28 February 2027, in three stages.
Grand finale: February 2027.

details.heading: Prize pool
details.body: Rs 5 crore across winners and prototype developers at the different stages.

items.name: NIDAR 2027
items.description: India's largest national drone innovation challenge, with three problem statements and a Rs 67 lakh prize pool.

details.heading: Organiser
details.body: Hosted by Drone Federation India with the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY), under the SwaYaan initiative. The 2026–27 edition was launched on 13 July 2026 in New Delhi.

details.heading: Problem statements
details.body:
Rescue Swarm
Air Mouse
VEGA Pilot

details.heading: Format
details.body: Hybrid and multi-stage: online submissions and evaluations, followed by an in-person final operational round.

details.heading: Duration
details.body: 1 August 2026 – 31 August 2027, held nationwide.

details.heading: Skills tested
details.body: Drone autonomy, computer vision, onboard sensing, navigation, control and real-time decision-making.

details.heading: Prize pool
details.body: Rs 67 lakh.

details.heading: Official website
details.body: nidar.org.in

items.name: SAUVC 2027
items.description: International student underwater robotics challenge: build an AUV to complete four tasks in a pool.

details.heading: Organiser
details.body: IEEE OES Singapore, supported by the National University of Singapore and Singapore Polytechnic.

details.heading: Scale
details.body: Now in its 11th year, with participants from 25 countries who have built 126 autonomous underwater vehicles.

details.heading: The four challenges
details.body:
Navigation
Visual identification
Acoustic localisation
Robotic manipulation
Performance is judged on speed and accuracy.

details.heading: Team rules
details.body: Teams may have up to 11 members, and at least half must be non-professionals (students, hobbyists or hackerspace members) at registration. Detailed rules are in Rulebook v6.1.0.

details.heading: Dates and venue
details.body: 24–27 February 2027 at Singapore Polytechnic, Singapore.

details.heading: Beyond the competition
details.body: Mentorship, skill development across mechanical, electrical and software engineering, guest lectures from marine robotics experts, and networking.

details.heading: Official website
details.body: sauvc.org

items.name: ROBOCON 2027
items.description: India's national robotics championship and the qualifier for ABU Robocon 2027 in Indonesia.

details.heading: Organisers
details.body: IIT Delhi, Prasar Bharati (Doordarshan) and STPI.

details.heading: Purpose
details.body: DD Robocon India is the exclusive national qualifier for ABU Robocon 2027. The winning team represents India at the international final in Solo, Indonesia.

details.heading: 2027 theme
details.body: “The Pursuit of Mustika Nusantara” — robots must master complex physical tasks under strict time limits.

details.heading: Stages and dates
details.body:
31 Dec 2026: pre-registration opens.
31 Jan 2027: concept note and idea submission deadline.
15 Feb 2027: Stage 1 shortlisting announced.
15 May 2027: Stage 2 video submission deadline.
31 May 2027: Stage 2 shortlisting results.
1–4 Jul 2027: DD Robocon national final.

details.heading: ABU Robocon 2027
details.body: 29 August 2027 at Edutorium UMS, Surakarta (Solo), Central Java, Indonesia.

details.heading: Official website
details.body: ddrobocon.iitd.ac.in

items.title: GUJCOST Robofest 5.0 — 14 Teams Qualified for Level-2, Highest in India
items.detail: 14 teams from TRS BVM advanced to Level-2 of Robofest 5.0 -- the highest number of teams selected from a single institution across the nation. Out of 1,102 ideation proposals submitted in Level-1 (914 at Senior Level), only 138 senior-level proposals were shortlisted for Level-2, and 14 of those were from BVM. Each advancing team received Rs 50,000. Categories: Underwater (Dr. A. A. Vahora, Dr. A. M. Thakkar, Prof. G. B. Rathod, Prof. V. J. Patel, Dr. M. S. Holia), Aerial (Prof. V. R. Singh), Maze (Dr. M. S. Holia), IGV (Prof. V. J. Patel, Prof. H. P. Patolia), Application (Prof. D. M. Patel, Prof. H. P. Patolia, Prof. D. K. Patel, Dr. M. M. Solanki, Prof. J. R. Koisa).

explore.heading: We compete, we learn, we grow

about.text: TRS BVM is the authorised student chapter of The Robotics Society (TRS), India, at BVM Engineering College. The Robotics Society empowers technical institutions across India to start TRS Student Chapters — a group of researchers, industrialists and students working in different domains of robotics, together making our society.

Regular meetings help us connect with every member and keep everyone updated with the latest technology, because we believe that technology will not replace great teachers, but technology in the hands of great teachers is transformational.
We believe that any sufficiently advanced technology is equivalent to magic. That magic shows in our projects, built with the help of faculty and M.Tech students.
We are a team not because we work together, but because we respect each other and welcome every member's ideas and projects from their innovative minds.
